title: JRE 2283 - Billy Corgan
guestBio: Billy Corgan is the lead singer of The Smashing Pumpkins and host of "The Magnificent Others" podcast. The Smashing Pumpkins' latest album, "Aghori Mhori Me," is available now.
tldr: Billy Corgan discusses The Smashing Pumpkins' reunion and creative process over the years
Conversation about the music industry, streaming, and how it has changed since the band's peak
Billy shares insights on his podcast 'The Magnificent Others' and interviewing other artists
Discussion of the new album 'Aghori Mhori Me' and the band's current direction
Billy reflects on fame, legacy, and the pressures of being a rock icon
Exploration of creative spirituality and how it influences his songwriting
recap:
Joe sits down with Billy Corgan, the iconic frontman of The Smashing Pumpkins, in what turns out to be a deep dive into music, legacy, and the creative process. Billy is there to talk about the band's latest album, 'Aghori Mhori Me,' and how The Smashing Pumpkins continue to evolve after all these years in the industry.

The conversation naturally flows into how the music industry has transformed since The Smashing Pumpkins' peak in the 90s. Billy talks about streaming, how artists make money now, and the weird relationship musicians have with their own catalog in the digital age. He's refreshingly honest about the business side of rock and roll, the way record labels operated back then versus now, and what it means to be a legacy artist trying to stay relevant.

Billy also discusses his podcast 'The Magnificent Others' and what drives him to interview other creative people. He seems genuinely interested in understanding how other artists think and work, which comes across as authentic curiosity rather than just another celebrity vanity project. The conversation touches on spirituality and how it informs his creative work, which for Billy isn't just about the music but about tapping into something deeper.

Throughout the episode, there's a thread about pressure and expectations. Being in one of the biggest rock bands of all time comes with a certain weight that never really goes away. Billy reflects on fame and whether the legacy he's built with The Smashing Pumpkins feels like a blessing or a burden, and he's not afraid to get real about the struggles of maintaining creative momentum while people want you to basically recreate what you did 20 or 30 years ago.

The vibe is conversational and goes places you'd expect from a Joe and musician interview, with plenty of tangents but always circling back to what drives creative people and how they make sense of their place in the world.
